\smallskip\noindent\textbf{DQM and envelope.}
For fixed \(n,\varepsilon,M,c_0\), and \(\Delta\tau>0\), there is a common
physical one-sided neighbourhood \(\mathcal Q^+\) of
\(\mathcal C_n(\varepsilon,M,c_0)\), in the coordinates
\(q=(\eta,\delta)\), on which \(c\pm\sqrt\delta>0\) and, for every
multi-index \(a\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log g_q(k)|
 &\le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},&& 1\le|a|\le3,\\
 \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log S_q(k)|
 &\le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},&& 1\le|a|\le2.
\end{aligned}
\]
All parameter derivatives extend continuously to \(\delta=0\), and
\(g_q(k)\le C(1+k)^{n-1}r^k\) for a common \(r<1\).  Writing
\(e_q(a)=S_q(a)/\mu_q\), the families \(g_q\) and \(e_q\) are uniformly
differentiable in quadratic mean.  Uniformly over base points on the collision
stratum and bounded physical root-\(N\) local arrays \(q_N\),
\[
 H^2(g_{q_N},g_{q_0})=O(N^{-1}),\qquad
 H^2(e_{q_N},e_{q_0})=O(N^{-1}),\qquad
 |\mu_{q_N}-\mu_{q_0}|=O(N^{-1/2}).
\]

\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Stopped-score CLT and information LLN.}
Let \(\mathcal Q\) be compact and let the integer Palm gaps \(G\) have full
support, a common exponential moment, and parameter-continuous masses.  Let a
stationary binary renewal record of length \(N\) contain \(K_N\) complete
gaps, with initial forward recurrence \(A_N\) and terminal backward recurrence
\(R_N\), and put \(D=G+1\), \(\mu_q=\EE_qD\).  Uniformly in
\(q\in\mathcal Q\), and for triangular arrays \(q_N\in\mathcal Q\),
\[
 K_N=N/\mu_{q_N}+O_{P_{q_N}}(\sqrt N),\qquad
 \max\{A_N,R_N,G_1,\ldots,G_{K_N}\}=O_{P_{q_N}}(\log N).
\]
If \(b_q(G)\in\RR^d\) is parameter-continuous, \(\EE_qb_q(G)=0\), and is
bounded by a common polynomial in \(G\), then
\[
 \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q}d_{\rm BL}\!\left(
 \mathcal L_q\!\left[N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}b_q(G_j)\right],
 \mathcal N_d\!\left(0,\mu_q^{-1}\EE_q[b_qb_q^\top]\right)
 \right)\longrightarrow0.
\]
For every similarly dominated matrix reward \(H_q\),
\[
 N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}H_q(G_j)
 -\mu_q^{-1}\EE_qH_q(G)\longrightarrow0
\]
uniformly in probability.  If \(B_q\) has a common polynomial envelope, then
\[
 N^{-3/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}B_q(G_j)=o_P(1)
\]
uniformly.  These conclusions hold jointly and apply to the score, stopped
Hessian, and third-order likelihood remainder under bounded root-\(N\) local
triangular arrays.

\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Plug-in equicontinuity.}
On the canonically ordered collision stratum, write the one-cycle null scores
as \(s_\eta\) and \(s_\delta\), and define
\[
 \psi_\eta=s_\delta-I_{\delta\eta}I_{\eta\eta}^{-1}s_\eta,
 \qquad
 \Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta)=N^{-1/2}
 \sum_{j=1}^{K_N}\psi_\eta(G_j).
\]
For every fixed \(L<\infty\),
\[
 \sup_\eta\sup_{\|\eta'-\eta\|\le L/\sqrt N}
 |\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta')-\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta)|
 =o_{P_{\eta,0}}(1).
\]
The conclusion also holds under bounded contiguous local alternatives.  The
empirical calendar information and its Schur complement, evaluated anywhere
in the same root-\(N\) ball, converge uniformly to \(I_n(\eta)\) and
\(J_n(\eta)\).  Hence any measurable root-\(N\) null fit may be inserted in
the standardized efficient central sequence with an \(o_P(1)\) change.

 219: \subsection{Limit experiment, efficient testing, and recovery}
 220: 
 221: \begin{theorem}[Stationary isolated-double-pole limit experiment]
 222: \label{thm:stationary-serial-double-pole-main}
 223: Fix \(n,\varepsilon,M,c_0\), known \(\Delta\tau>0\), and the serial positive
 224: killed-reset realization \textup{(1.2)}--\textup{(1.3)}, and suppose
 225: \(\mathcal C_n(\varepsilon,M,c_0)\ne\varnothing\).  Let
 226: \(P_{\eta,\delta}^{(N)}\) be the stationary length-\(N\) binary renewal
 227: record in this fixed serial order, at one isolated real double pole with all
 228: other rates simple and separated as in \textup{(3.1)}.
 229: 
 230: \smallskip\noindent\textup{(A) Uniform LAN and the limit experiment.}
 231: For bounded \(u\in\RR^{n-1}\) and \(v\in[0,\infty)\), uniformly over the
 232: collision stratum,
 233: \[
 234:  \log\frac{dP_{\eta_0+u/\sqrt N,v/\sqrt N}^{(N)}}
 235:  {dP_{\eta_0,0}^{(N)}}
 236:  =\begin{pmatrix}u\\v\end{pmatrix}^{\!\top}\Delta_{N,\eta_0}
 237:  -\frac12\begin{pmatrix}u\\v\end{pmatrix}^{\!\top}
 238:  I_n(\eta_0)\begin{pmatrix}u\\v\end{pmatrix}
 239:  +o_{P_{\eta_0,0}}(1),
 240: \tag{3.15}
 241: \]
 242: where
 243: \(\Delta_{N,\eta_0}\Rightarrow\mathcal N_n\{0,I_n(\eta_0)\}\)
 244: uniformly in bounded-Lipschitz distance.  The local experiments converge to
 245: the Gaussian shift on \(\RR^{n-1}\times[0,\infty)\), and the information is
 246: uniformly nondegenerate by \textup{(3.5)}.
 247: 
 248: \smallskip\noindent\textup{(B) Efficient collision test.}
 249: Partition \(I_n\) according to \((\eta,\delta)\) and set
 250: \[
 251:  J_n(\eta)=I_{\delta\delta}
 252:  -I_{\delta\eta}I_{\eta\eta}^{-1}I_{\eta\delta}>0.
 253: \tag{3.16}
 254: \]
 255: The residualized-score test \(\phi_N\) in \textup{(3.14)} has uniform
 256: asymptotic level \(\alpha\).  At
 257: \((\eta_N,\delta_N)=(\eta_0+u/\sqrt N,v/\sqrt N)\), its limiting power is
 258: \[
 259:  1-\Phi_{\rm N}\{z_{1-\alpha}-v\sqrt{J_n(\eta_0)}\}.
 260: \tag{3.17}
 261: \]
 262: This is the Gaussian half-space power envelope among tests with uniform local
 263: asymptotic level \(\alpha\).
 264: 
 265: \smallskip\noindent\textup{(C) Attainable and lower recovery rates.}
 266: The measurable procedure in \Cref{est:serial-collision-recurrence-main}
 267: gives root-\(N\) estimates of \(\eta\) and \(\delta\) and an induced rate
 268: multiset \(\widehat{\mathcal R}_{n,N}\) satisfying
 269: \[
 270:  d_{\rm m}\!\left(\widehat{\mathcal R}_{n,N},
 271:  \{\!\{c_N+\sqrt{\delta_N},c_N-\sqrt{\delta_N},
 272:  \theta_{3,N},\ldots,\theta_{n,N}\}\!\}\right)=O_P(N^{-1/4})
 273: \tag{3.18}
 274: \]
 275: uniformly over the compact stratum and bounded \((u,v)\).  The centre and
 276: canonically ordered separated rates remain root-\(N\).  At every fixed base,
 277: \Cref{lem:two-point-threshold-rate-main} gives a strictly positive lower
 278: limit for threshold risk on two alternatives separated by
 279: \(\sqrt{v_0}N^{-1/4}\).  Hence \(N^{-1/4}\) is uniformly attainable on the
 280: stated bounded local families and pointwise locally minimax-optimal in rate.
 281: \end{theorem}
 282: 
 283: \begin{corollary}[The two-state collision]
 284: \label{cor:two-state-collision-main}
 285: For \(n=2\), the stratum restrictions on separated rates are vacuous and
 286: \Cref{thm:stationary-serial-double-pole-main} applies with \(\eta=c\).  In
 287: particular,
 288: \[
 289:  \mathcal L\{\overline F_{c,\delta}\}(s)
 290:  =\frac1s\left\{1-\frac{c^2-\delta}{(s+c)^2-\delta}\right\},
 291: \quad
 292:  \left.\partial_\delta\mathcal L\{\overline F_{c,\delta}\}(s)
 293:  \right|_0=\frac{s+2c}{(s+c)^4},
 294: \tag{3.19}
 295: \]
 296: whereas the centre derivative is \(-2c/(s+c)^3\).  Thus the stationary
 297: two-state record has the Gaussian half-plane experiment on
 298: \(\RR\times[0,\infty)\), the residualized test has power
 299: \(1-\Phi_{\rm N}\{z_{1-\alpha}-v\sqrt{J_2(c)}\}\), and the unordered pair
 300: is recoverable at the matching upper and fixed-base two-point lower rate
 301: \(N^{-1/4}\).  The sign of the rate split is not identifiable.
 302: \end{corollary}
 303: 
 304: \begin{proof}
 305: This is the specialization of \Cref{thm:stationary-serial-double-pole-main}
 306: with the empty product \(B_\eta=1\).  Direct differentiation of
 307: \textup{(3.19)} gives the displayed fourth- and third-order poles.  Detailed
 308: two-state tail, recurrence, score, and estimator calculations are recorded in
 309: \Cref*{sec:two-state-calculations-supp} of the supplementary material.
 310: \end{proof}
 311: 
 312: \begin{lemma}[Two-point threshold-risk lower bound]
 313: \label{lem:two-point-threshold-rate-main}
 314: Fix a collision base \((\eta_0,0)\), hold \(\eta_0\) fixed, and compare
 315: \(P_{0,N}=P_{\eta_0,0}^{(N)}\) with
 316: \(P_{1,N}=P_{\eta_0,v_0/\sqrt N}^{(N)}\), where \(v_0>0\).  Let their
 317: unordered rate multisets be \(\mathcal R_{0,N}\) and \(\mathcal R_{1,N}\),
 318: and put \(h_N=\sqrt{v_0}N^{-1/4}\).  For \(n=2\) their matching distance is
 319: exactly \(h_N\) whenever the alternative is admissible.  For \(n>2\), the
 320: same equality holds whenever \(h_N<c_0/2\), in particular for all sufficiently
 321: large \(N\).  For every \(0<a<\sqrt{v_0}/2\),
 322: \[
 323:  \liminf_{N\to\infty}\inf_{\widehat{\mathcal R}_N}
 324:  \max_{i=0,1}P_{i,N}\!\left\{
 325:  N^{1/4}d_{\rm m}(\widehat{\mathcal R}_N,\mathcal R_{i,N})>a
 326:  \right\}
 327:  \ge \Phi_{\rm N}\!\left(
 328:  -\frac{v_0\sqrt{I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)}}2\right)>0.
 329: \tag{3.20}
 330: \]
 331: The conclusion is pointwise at a fixed base, uses two alternatives and
 332: threshold loss, and asserts optimality in rate rather than an exact minimax
 333: risk over a continuum.
 334: \end{lemma}
 335: 
 336: \begin{proof}
 337: Matching every unchanged separated rate to itself and the colliding entries to
 338: \(c-h_N\) and \(c+h_N\) gives distance at most \(h_N\).  If \(n>2\) and
 339: \(h_N<c_0/2\), every separated rate is at distance at least
 340: \(c_0-h_N>h_N\) from either perturbed collision entry, so no matching through
 341: a separated rate improves it.  The equality is immediate for \(n=2\).
 342: 
 343: The balls of radius \(aN^{-1/4}\) around the two candidates are disjoint.
 344: Assigning an estimate to its nearer candidate turns simultaneous estimation
 345: success into correct testing of \(P_{0,N}\) against \(P_{1,N}\).  Under
 346: \(P_{0,N}\), the LAN likelihood ratio converges to
 347: \[
 348:  \exp\{v_0Z-\tfrac12v_0^2I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)\},
 349:  \qquad Z\sim\mathcal N(0,I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)).
 350: \tag{3.21}
 351: \]
 352: Its limit has mean one, and mutual contiguity makes the likelihood ratios
 353: uniformly integrable.  Their total-variation distances therefore converge to
 354: that of the two Gaussian shifts separated by
 355: \(v_0\sqrt{I_{\delta\delta}(\eta_0)}\).  The maximum error of any test is at
 356: least its equal-prior average error, whose limiting infimum is the right side
 357: of \textup{(3.20)}.  Taking a measurable estimator within \(o(1)\) of the
 358: infimum at each \(N\) proves the bound.
 359: \end{proof}

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Deterministic algebra checks for the renewal collision article."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import math
from pathlib import Path


def tail_two_rate(k: int, rate_a: float, rate_b: float, dt: float) -> float:
    if abs(rate_a - rate_b) < 1e-12:
        x = rate_a * dt * k
        return (1.0 + x) * math.exp(-x)
    return (
        rate_a * math.exp(-rate_b * dt * k)
        - rate_b * math.exp(-rate_a * dt * k)
    ) / (rate_a - rate_b)


def recurrence_residual(values: list[float], roots: list[float]) -> float:
    if len(roots) != 2:
        raise ValueError("the regression helper checks order two")
    root_sum = roots[0] + roots[1]
    root_product = roots[0] * roots[1]
    return max(
        abs(values[k + 2] - root_sum * values[k + 1] + root_product * values[k])
        for k in range(len(values) - 2)
    )


def checks() -> list[tuple[str, bool, str]]:
    dt = 0.7
    rate_a, rate_b = 1.1, 2.3
    z_a, z_b = math.exp(-rate_a * dt), math.exp(-rate_b * dt)
    tails = [tail_two_rate(k, rate_a, rate_b, dt) for k in range(8)]

    common = 1.4
    z = math.exp(-common * dt)
    confluent = [tail_two_rate(k, common, common, dt) for k in range(8)]
    x = common * dt
    hankel_det = confluent[0] * confluent[2] - confluent[1] ** 2

    c = 1.7
    delta = 0.09
    pair = (c + math.sqrt(delta), c - math.sqrt(delta))
    sampled = [math.exp(-value * dt) for value in pair]
    cluster_a = sampled[0] + sampled[1]
    cluster_b = sampled[0] * sampled[1]
    recovered_c = -math.log(cluster_b) / (2.0 * dt)
    recovered_delta = (
        math.acosh(cluster_a / (2.0 * math.sqrt(cluster_b))) / dt
    ) ** 2

    gamma = 0.75
    undershoot_ratio = 10_000 ** gamma / 10_000
    fluctuation_ratio = 10_000 ** gamma / math.sqrt(10_000)

    p = math.exp(-rate_a * dt)
    s = math.exp(-rate_b * dt)
    b = rate_b * math.exp(-rate_a * dt) * (
        1.0 - math.exp(-(rate_b - rate_a) * dt)
    ) / (rate_b - rate_a)
    a = 1.0 - s - b

    return [
        ("two-rate tail starts at one", abs(tails[0] - 1.0) < 1e-14, f"S0={tails[0]:.16g}"),
        ("two-rate tail decreases", all(tails[i] > tails[i + 1] > 0 for i in range(7)), f"S7={tails[-1]:.6g}"),
        ("simple-root recurrence", recurrence_residual(tails, [z_a, z_b]) < 1e-13, "order-2 residual"),
        ("confluent tail formula", abs(confluent[3] - (1 + 3 * x) * z**3) < 1e-14, "equal-rate limit"),
        ("double-root recurrence", recurrence_residual(confluent, [z, z]) < 1e-13, "repeated root"),
        ("collision Hankel invertible", abs(hankel_det) > 1e-6, f"det={hankel_det:.6g}"),
        ("cluster centre recovery", abs(recovered_c - c) < 1e-13, f"c={recovered_c:.15g}"),
        ("cluster square recovery", abs(recovered_delta - delta) < 1e-13, f"delta={recovered_delta:.15g}"),
        ("undershoot sublinear", undershoot_ratio < 0.2, f"ratio={undershoot_ratio:.6g}"),
        ("undershoot exceeds root-N scale", fluctuation_ratio > 5.0, f"ratio={fluctuation_ratio:.6g}"),
        ("two-state zero kernel substochastic", 0 < p < 1 and 0 < s < 1 and b > 0 and a > 0, f"a={a:.6g}, b={b:.6g}"),
        ("marked reset is rank one", abs((1 - p) * a - a * (1 - p)) < 1e-15, "both marked rows end in D"),
    ]


def render() -> str:
    rows = checks()
    failed = [name for name, ok, _ in rows if not ok]
    lines = ["Renewal equivalence and double-pole verification"]
    lines.extend(f"{'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}  {name}: {detail}" for name, ok, detail in rows)
    lines.append(f"Summary: {len(rows) - len(failed)}/{len(rows)} checks passed")
    if failed:
        raise AssertionError(", ".join(failed))
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    report = render()
    if args.output:
        args.output.write_text(report, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
    print(report, end="")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import math
import unittest

import verify_claims as verify


class RenewalCollisionChecks(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_all_report_checks_pass(self):
        self.assertTrue(all(ok for _, ok, _ in verify.checks()))

    def test_report_count(self):
        self.assertEqual(len(verify.checks()), 12)

    def test_report_summary(self):
        self.assertIn("Summary: 12/12 checks passed", verify.render())

    def test_unequal_tail_at_zero(self):
        self.assertAlmostEqual(verify.tail_two_rate(0, 0.8, 1.6, 0.5), 1.0)

    def test_equal_tail_at_zero(self):
        self.assertAlmostEqual(verify.tail_two_rate(0, 1.2, 1.2, 0.5), 1.0)

    def test_equal_tail_formula(self):
        expected = (1 + 1.2) * math.exp(-1.2)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(verify.tail_two_rate(2, 1.2, 1.2, 0.5), expected)

    def test_unequal_tail_positive(self):
        self.assertGreater(verify.tail_two_rate(10, 0.8, 1.6, 0.5), 0.0)

    def test_unequal_tail_decreasing(self):
        values = [verify.tail_two_rate(k, 0.8, 1.6, 0.5) for k in range(10)]
        self.assertTrue(all(a > b for a, b in zip(values, values[1:])))

    def test_simple_recurrence(self):
        dt = 0.5
        values = [verify.tail_two_rate(k, 0.8, 1.6, dt) for k in range(10)]
        roots = [math.exp(-0.8 * dt), math.exp(-1.6 * dt)]
        self.assertLess(verify.recurrence_residual(values, roots), 1e-13)

    def test_double_recurrence(self):
        dt = 0.5
        values = [verify.tail_two_rate(k, 1.2, 1.2, dt) for k in range(10)]
        root = math.exp(-1.2 * dt)
        self.assertLess(verify.recurrence_residual(values, [root, root]), 1e-13)

    def test_recurrence_requires_two_roots(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            verify.recurrence_residual([1.0, 0.5, 0.25], [0.5])

    def test_matching_scale(self):
        v0, n = 4.0, 10_000
        self.assertAlmostEqual(math.sqrt(v0) * n ** (-0.25), 0.2)

    def test_projection_nonexpansive_positive(self):
        x, y = -0.03, 0.04
        self.assertLessEqual(abs(max(x, 0.0) - y), abs(x - y))

    def test_square_root_inequality(self):
        x, y = 0.01, 0.04
        self.assertLessEqual(abs(math.sqrt(x) - math.sqrt(y)), math.sqrt(abs(x - y)))

    def test_gamma_range(self):
        gamma = 0.75
        self.assertTrue(0.5 < gamma < 1.0)

    def test_calendar_information_scale(self):
        palm_information, mean = 3.0, 2.5
        self.assertAlmostEqual(palm_information / mean, 1.2)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

 transfers every null \(o_P(1)\) assertion to bounded local alternatives.
 \end{proof}

+\tag{U11}\label{eq:u11-supp}
 \]
 Differentiating the first identity, justified by
 \Cref{lem:uniform-sampled-bin-tail-score-main}, gives
 \[
  \EE_{\eta,0}(\partial_\eta\psi_\eta)
  =-\EE_{\eta,0}(\psi_\eta s_\eta^\top)=0.
-\tag{U12}
+\tag{U12}\label{eq:u12-supp}
 \]
 Thus the derivative of \(\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}\) is a normalized stopped sum
 of centred rewards and is \(O_P(1)\) uniformly by
 \Cref{lem:uniform-stopped-renewal-score-main}.  A second-order Taylor expansion
 over a ball of radius \(L/\sqrt N\) has first term \(O_P(N^{-1/2})\); its
 second term is bounded by
-\(N^{-1/2}O_P(N)O(N^{-1})=O_P(N^{-1/2})\).  This proves \textup{(U10)}.
+\(N^{-1/2}O_P(N)O(N^{-1})=O_P(N^{-1/2})\).  This proves \eqref{eq:u10-supp}.
 The stopped LLN applied to score outer products, followed by the same Taylor
 bound and continuity of matrix inversion on the uniformly positive-definite
 set, proves information consistency.  The normalization and the two
 stationary endpoint log-score increments obey the same conclusion: their parameter
 increments are bounded by \(N^{-1/2}\) times a polynomial in
-\(\max(A_N,R_N)\), which is \(O_P(\log N)\) by \textup{(U6)}.  Thus they
+\(\max(A_N,R_N)\), which is \(O_P(\log N)\) by \eqref{eq:u6-supp}.  Thus they
 contribute \(o_P(1)\) uniformly to the plug-in difference.  Contiguity
 transfers every null \(o_P(1)\) assertion to bounded local alternatives.
 \end{proof}

 Thus the derivative of \(\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}\) is a normalized stopped sum
 of centred rewards and is \(O_P(1)\) uniformly by
 \Cref{lem:uniform-stopped-renewal-score-main}.  A second-order Taylor expansion
 over a ball of radius \(L/\sqrt N\) has first term \(O_P(N^{-1/2})\); its
 second term is bounded by
-\(N^{-1/2}O_P(N)O(N^{-1})=O_P(N^{-1/2})\).  This proves \textup{(U10)}.
+\(N^{-1/2}O_P(N)O(N^{-1})=O_P(N^{-1/2})\).  This proves \eqref{eq:u10-supp}.
 The stopped LLN applied to score outer products, followed by the same Taylor
 bound and continuity of matrix inversion on the uniformly positive-definite
 set, proves information consistency.  The normalization and the two
 stationary endpoint log-score increments obey the same conclusion: their parameter
 increments are bounded by \(N^{-1/2}\) times a polynomial in
-\(\max(A_N,R_N)\), which is \(O_P(\log N)\) by \textup{(U6)}.  Thus they
+\(\max(A_N,R_N)\), which is \(O_P(\log N)\) by \eqref{eq:u6-supp}.  Thus they
 contribute \(o_P(1)\) uniformly to the plug-in difference.  Contiguity
 transfers every null \(o_P(1)\) assertion to bounded local alternatives.
 \end{proof}

-\(\max(A_N,R_N)\), which is \(O_P(\log N)\) by \textup{(U6)}.  Thus they
+\(\max(A_N,R_N)\), which is \(O_P(\log N)\) by \eqref{eq:u6-supp}.  Thus they
 contribute \(o_P(1)\) uniformly to the plug-in difference.  Contiguity
 transfers every null \(o_P(1)\) assertion to bounded local alternatives.
 \end{proof}
